question: Which traveller from Uzbekistan visited India in the 11th Century?
solution:
The correct answer is **Alberuni**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Al-Biruni wrote Kitab-Ul-Hind and it was written in Arabic.
 
• Al-Biruni spent years in the company of Brahmana priests and scholars, learning Sanskrit, and studying religious and philosophical texts.
 
• He translated several Sanskrit works, including Patanjali’s work on grammar, into Arabic.
 
• Al-Biruni’s Kitab-ul-Hind, written in Arabic, is simple and lucid.
 
• It is a voluminous text, divided into 80 chapters on subjects such as religion and philosophy, festivals, astronomy, alchemy, manners and customs, social life, weights and measures, iconography, laws and metrology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Seydi Ali Reis **was **an Ottoman admiral **and **navigator**. Known also as **Katib-i Rumi. **He commanded the **left wing of the Ottoman fleet **at the **naval Battle **of **Preveza in 1538**.
 
• **Abu Abdullah Muhammad ibn Battutah **was a **Berber Maghrebi scholar **and **explorer **who **travelled extensively **in the **lands of Afro-Eurasia, largely in the Muslim world**.
 
• **Mahmud bin Amir Ali Balkhi**, a **Central Asian **traveler to **India **in **Jahangir’s reign **was **horrified **to see **a group of 23 Muslims **in **Banaras **who had **deserted their religion **and **turned Hindu.**
